description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994, idiom 29), narrowed to ONE line.  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/json1.pl, bitand2.pl):
  use JSON::PP; my $j = JSON::PP->new->canonical;
  print $j->encode([1, 2.5, "s", 1+1]);              perl [1,2.5,"s",2]        PCL ["1","2.5","s","2"]
  print $j->encode($j->decode('{"a":[1,2.5]}'));     perl {"a":[1,2.5]}        PCL {"a":["1","2.5"]}
  my $n = 5; my $f = 2.5; my $s = "abc"; my $u = "\x{263a}";
  utf8::is_utf8($n), ($f), ($s), ($u)                perl 0 0 0 1              PCL 1 1 1 1

THE MECHANISM (measured): JSON::PP::_looks_like_number (USE_B is 0 by default) is
    return if utf8::is_utf8($value);
    return unless length((my $dummy = "") & $value);   # "" & number = 0 (numeric and), "" & string = ""
    return unless 0 + $value eq $value;
    return 1 if $value * 0 == 0;
and the function copied WITHOUT its first line answers 1 for 5, 2.5, 1+1 under PCL exactly as under perl (probe bitand1.pl).  So the ONLY thing between PCL and a correct JSON::PP is `pl-is_utf8` = `(declare (ignore str)) 1` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp).

THIS DOES NOT REOPEN THE RULED DIVERGENCE (#1389, not-supported.md "The per-scalar UTF-8 flag", RULED s473h): that ruling is about STRINGS -- "every PCL string IS in the upgraded form, so 1 is the honest answer".  A value that is not a string at all (a CL integer / float / ratio, undef, a reference, a code ref, a glob) has no character form to be upgraded, and perl answers FALSE for every one of them (probe first: is_utf8(5), (2.5), (undef), (\1), ([]), (sub {}), a number that was stringified once `my $n = 5; "$n"; is_utf8($n)`, a dualvar-ish `$s = "7"; $s + 0; is_utf8($s)`).  FIX SHAPE: `pl-is_utf8` answers perl's false for a non-string value and stays 1 for every string.  One function; rule 12 does not apply (it is a total predicate).  Update the not-supported.md entry with the narrowed statement and ir-spec where is_utf8 is described.

WHY IT MATTERS: JSON::PP is on the README's module list and is how every script without JSON::XS emits JSON; numbers as strings breaks every typed consumer.  The `json-rt` bench row is "verified against perl" -- find out how it passes with this bug (it may compare a shape without numbers) and say so in the DONE section; if its verification is blind to the number/string distinction, widen it.

BAR: runtime-only (`cl/`) => full sweep + the companion legs that call is_utf8 (`grep -a -l is_utf8` under perl's t/: lib/ uni/ op/ -- run the ones the snapshot lists) + `tools/ir-conform --jobs 2` (known-fail row `243-string` is #1389's and must NOT move) + guard rows in an existing Pl/t file (json-pp or utf8): the JSON::PP encode/decode rows above with perl as the oracle, INVERSE-verified.  CPAN board: the JSON-using dists by ROWS.


=== DONE (s492a) ===
SHIPPED 605c2067.  ONE function in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp: `pl-is_utf8` is now
`(p-bool (stringp (unbox str)))`, so the REPRESENTATION decides.  Every STRING
still answers 1, so the #1389 ruling stands; a number, a float, undef, a
reference and a code ref answer false, as perl does (21 shapes probed vs
5.40.3, scratch/s492a/probes/m1-isutf8.{pl,perl.out,base.out,tree.out}).

WHY IT WAS LOAD-BEARING: core JSON::PP's `_looks_like_number` starts
`return if utf8::is_utf8($value)`, so PCL encoded EVERY NUMBER AS A JSON
STRING.  `encode([1,2.5])` was `["1","2.5"]`, now `[1,2.5]`.

The task's json-rt bench question, answered: that row could NOT have caught
this -- its document is all strings by construction.  Its comment now says so
and points at the guard; the document itself is left alone because it is a
performance series (tools/bench-exec.pl).  Bench control BENCH_K=5: 1.73x vs
base 1.83x, no slowdown.

Guard Pl/t/is-utf8-01.t, 6 rows, 6/6 FAIL on a 268d7e00 extraction
(scratch/s492a/inverse-guards-base268.log).  The documented divergence
(`my $s = "7"; $s + 0` -- perl keeps the SV a string, PCL holds a number) is
cited in docs/not-supported.md's per-scalar-UTF-8-flag entry, not chased.

CORRECTION (s493 final bar): the acceptance probe's captured output on disk
was STALE (taken 14:59, before this member and member 3 landed).  Re-run on
the shipped tree, ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/json1.pl differs from perl in
TWO places, not one: row 5's `$s`-was-numified element (the documented SV-flag
divergence the brief named) AND row 6, a decode/encode round trip, where a
decoded INTEGER re-encodes as a STRING.  The second is a SECOND CAUSE, not
this one: JSON::PP computes `$max_intsize` in a BEGIN block by asking whether
a growing integer LITERAL stringifies with an exponent, PCL's integer literals
are exact bignums so it never does, `$max_intsize` stays undef, and
`length $v > undef` sends every decoded integer down the `return "$v"` branch.
This member's fix is what makes the FLOAT and EXPONENT forms right; the
integer half is FILED as #2016 with the measurement and three fix shapes.
subject: EVERYDAY (JSON::PP): `utf8::is_utf8` answers 1 for a NON-STRING (a number, undef, a reference) -- so core JSON::PP 4.16 encodes EVERY NUMBER AS A STRING (`encode([1, 2.5])` is `["1","2.5"]`, perl `[1,2.5]`), because its `_looks_like_number` starts with `return if utf8::is_utf8($value)`
